import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm, t, skewnorm

strategies = [
    ("Late-game 4th down aggression", "normal", {"mu":1.2, "sigma":0.5102}),
    ("Heavy pre-snap motion", "normal", {"mu":0.9, "sigma":0.4592}),
    ("Two-high safeties on early downs", "normal", {"mu":0.7, "sigma":0.5102}),
    ("Intentional safety before punt", "skew_normal", {"xi":-0.5, "omega":1.5, "alpha":2.0}),
    ("No-huddle against tired defenses", "skew_normal", {"xi":-0.3, "omega":1.3, "alpha":2.5}),
    ("Press-man coverage against slow receivers", "student_t", {"nu":4, "mu":0.5, "sigma":0.5403})
]

x = np.linspace(-5, 5, 1000)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 10))
for ax, (title, family, params) in zip(axes.flatten(), strategies):
    if family == "normal":
        mu = params["mu"]; sigma = params["sigma"]
        pdf = norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)
        low, high = norm.ppf(0.025, mu, sigma), norm.ppf(0.975, mu, sigma)
        most_plaus = mu
    elif family == "student_t":
        nu = params["nu"]; mu = params["mu"]; sigma = params["sigma"]
        pdf = t.pdf(x, nu, mu, sigma)
        low, high = t.ppf(0.025, nu, mu, sigma), t.ppf(0.975, nu, mu, sigma)
        most_plaus = mu
    elif family == "skew_normal":
        xi = params["xi"]; omega = params["omega"]; alpha = params["alpha"]
        pdf = skewnorm.pdf(x, alpha, xi, omega)
        low, high = skewnorm.ppf(0.025, alpha, xi, omega), skewnorm.ppf(0.975, alpha, xi, omega)
        # compute mode numerically from pdf
        mode_idx = np.argmax(pdf)
        most_plaus = x[mode_idx]
    ax.plot(x, pdf)
    ax.axvline(most_plaus, color='red', linestyle='--', label=f'Most plausible = {most_plaus:.3f}')
    ax.axvspan(low, high, alpha=0.3, color='gray', label=f'95% interval [{low:.3f}, {high:.3f}]')
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Change in own scoring margin (points)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

for title, family, params in strategies:
    print(f"{title}: family={family}, params={params}")

strategies.rationale: Wearing down a defense that is already fatigued can create scoring opportunities late in drives, boosting overall scoring margin beyond what conventional models capture.
strategies.recommendation: Employ an up-tempo no-huddle offense even when not trailing, specifically when the defense has been on the field for multiple consecutive drives. Intuition: speed of play prevents defensive substitutions and exhausts players, leading to missed assignments and easier gains. Analytics shows mixed results on turnovers and three-and-outs.

strategies.rationale: Taking away quick routes with physical coverage can force the offense to hold the ball longer, leading to sacks and stalled drives, increasing win probability.
strategies.recommendation: Against offenses with slow wide receivers (40-yard dash >4.6), play press-man coverage on early downs to disrupt release and timing. Intuition: press coverage's risk of being beaten deep is mitigated by lack of speed, and disruption forces incompletions or short gains. Analytics studies are mixed and don't account for specific receiver speed thresholds.
